title: You Are Invited to Max's Party
text:
Dear Friends,
You are invited to Max's seventh birthday party! It will be on Saturday at {number} o'clock in our backyard. Please wear something {adjective}, like a party hat or a pair of {plural noun}.

There will be lots of fun games. First we will play Pin the Tail on the {animal}. Then everyone will get a turn to {verb} in the bounce house. My dad says he will be {verb ending in ing} by the grill all afternoon, so come hungry!

For lunch we will have pizza, apple slices, and a giant bowl of {plural noun}. The cake is shaped like a {noun} and has {color} frosting on top.

Please do not bring a present that is too {adjective}. Max already has a lot of {plural noun}. Just bring yourself and a {adjective} smile!
Love,
Max's Mom

title: Thank You, Aunt Rosa
text:
Dear Aunt Rosa,
Thank you so much for the birthday present you sent me. When I opened the box, I found a {adjective} {noun} inside! I have always wanted one. Mom says it is the most {adjective} gift I have ever gotten.

I have used it every single day. On Monday, I took it to school and showed my teacher, Mrs. Green. She {past tense verb} so hard that she had to sit down. On Tuesday, my little brother tried to {verb} with it, and now he wants one too.

Also, thank you for the card with {number} dollars in it. I am saving it to buy a pet {animal} and a bag of {plural noun}.

I hope you can come to my next party. We will eat cake and dance {adverb} in the kitchen until {number} o'clock.
Love,
Sofia

title: Grandma's Famous Birthday Cake
text:
This is how my grandma makes my birthday cake every year. You will need a big bowl, a wooden spoon, and a grown-up helper.

First, mix two cups of flour with three {plural noun}. Stir it {adverb} until it looks {adjective}. Next, crack two eggs and add a spoonful of {food}. Grandma says this is the secret part, so do not tell anyone.

Pour everything into a pan and bake it for {number} minutes. While you wait, you can {verb} around the kitchen and sing to the oven. Grandma says the cake likes that.

When the cake is cool, cover it with {adjective} frosting and put a tiny {noun} on top. Add the candles and turn off the lights. Everyone will start {verb ending in ing} when they see it. Then they will say it is the most {adjective} cake in the whole world!

title: Rules for the Bounce House
text:
Welcome to the bounce house! Before you go in, please read these rules. My uncle Ted wrote them on a big piece of {color} paper and taped it to the door.

Rule one: Take off your shoes and your {plural noun}. Put them in the basket by the steps. Rule two: Only {number} kids can be inside at one time. If there are too many, the bounce house gets {adjective} and starts to wobble.

Rule three: No food inside. Last year my cousin brought a {noun} in with him, and we are still finding little pieces. Rule four: Please do not {verb} on the walls. Bouncing is fine. Jumping is fine. But {verb ending in ing} is not allowed, ever.

Rule five: If you feel {adjective}, come out and sit with Grandpa. He will give you a cup of water and a {adjective} {noun}. Have fun, bounce {adverb}, and remember to say thank you to the {plural noun}!

title: The Day I Turned Seven
text:
Dear Diary,
Today I turned seven! I woke up very early because my dog, Biscuit, was {verb ending in ing} on my bed. Mom made pancakes shaped like {plural noun} for breakfast. They were a little bit {adjective}, but I ate them all.

At school, my class sang the birthday song to me. My best friend Leo sang so {adverb} that the fish in our classroom tank hid behind a {noun}. Then I got to wear the special birthday crown. It is made of paper and {plural noun}.

After school, Grandpa came over with a present. It was a {adjective} {noun} with a big bow on top! I {past tense verb} around the living room three times.

Now I am in bed, and I am very tired. Being seven is {adjective}. Tomorrow I am going to {verb} all day long.

title: The Party Game Awards
text:
Here are the winners of today's party games. Every player did a great job, and nobody cried, not even once.

The Musical Chairs prize goes to Ava. She sat down so {adverb} that the chair made a squeaky sound. She wins a shiny {noun}. The Egg and Spoon Race was won by Jamal. He walked across the whole yard without dropping his egg, even when a {animal} ran in front of him. He wins {number} stickers and a bag of {plural noun}.

The Hula Hoop Contest ended in a tie. Mia and Ben kept {verb ending in ing} for ten whole minutes. Each of them gets a {adjective} medal.

Finally, the prize for Best Dancer goes to Grandpa Joe. He {past tense verb} across the patio and shook his {body part} like a {adjective} noodle. Next year, he says he will {verb} even better.

title: How to Blow Out Your Candles
text:
Blowing out birthday candles is a very important job. Here is how to do it the right way. First, wait until everyone has finished singing. Do not start early, or Aunt May will make everyone sing again, and she sings very {adverb}.

Next, close your eyes and make a wish. You can wish for anything you want, like a pet {animal} or a house made of {plural noun}. Keep your wish a secret!

Then take a deep breath. Fill your cheeks with air until they look like two {adjective} {plural noun}. Lean over the cake, but be careful not to put your {body part} in the frosting or bump the {noun} on top.

Now blow! If all the candles go out, everyone will clap and shout "{exclamation}!" If one candle stays lit, that is okay. Just try to {verb} a little harder. Last of all, the birthday kid gets the first piece. Eat it {adverb}!

title: Breaking News from the Backyard
text:
Good afternoon. This is Lily Park with breaking news from Oak Street, where a birthday party is happening right now. At one o'clock, the guests arrived carrying presents and {plural noun}. People say the birthday girl, Rosie, {past tense verb} at the front door and gave everyone a {adjective} hug.

At two o'clock, there was trouble. A big gust of wind blew the balloons into a tree. A tall neighbor got them down using only a ladder and a {noun}. The crowd cheered {adverb}.

At three o'clock, the piñata was finally opened. Out came candy, toys, and {number} tiny {plural noun}. Kids were seen {verb ending in ing} all over the grass.

Right now, the party is still going. Rosie's dad has asked everyone to {verb} before the ice cream melts. Experts say it is the most {adjective} party of the year. Back to you in the studio!

title: What Is in Your Party Bag
text:
Thank you for coming to Nora's birthday party! Here is a list of what is inside your party bag. One bouncy ball. Please do not bounce it inside, or your grown-up might get {adjective}. Two stickers shaped like {plural noun}. You can put them on your notebook or your {noun}.

Three pieces of candy. Nora picked these out herself. She says the {color} ones taste like {food}. One tiny jar of bubbles. To use it, dip the wand and blow {adverb}. If you blow too hard, you will just {verb} instead.

One paper crown. Wear it at dinner tonight and tell everyone you are the king or queen of {place}. One small surprise at the very bottom. Nora will not tell anyone what it is, but she says it might be {verb ending in ing} when you open the bag.

Thank you for being such a {adjective} guest. See you next year!

title: Dad's Party Checklist
text:
Dad made a checklist so that my birthday party goes perfectly. He wrote it with a {color} marker and hung it on the fridge with a magnet shaped like a {noun}.

First, he will blow up {number} balloons and tie them to the mailbox. Then he will hang a big sign that says Happy Birthday in {adjective} letters. Mom said the sign from last year was a little too {adjective}, so this year it will be smaller.

Next, he will set up the snack table. It will have juice boxes, cheese crackers, and a tall stack of {plural noun}. He will also practice {verb ending in ing} so he can be the party clown. He says he is getting very good at it.

Finally, at four o'clock, he will carry out the cake and sing {adverb}. Then he will sit on the couch, take off his {plural noun}, and {verb} for the rest of the day. That part is not on the list, but Mom says it always happens.
